subject: Negative variances and and not positive definite covariance matrix in a growth model

messages.author: 8d4d06c10c4d67c9
messages.subject: Negative variances and and not positive definite covariance matrix in a growth model
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to fit a growth model to my data and am getting these warnings:
Warning messages:
1: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: some estimated variances are negative
2: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.



I tried to make sure that I'm using laavan correctly so I simulated equivalent data which consists of:
Measurements of the time a mouse stays on a rod in three consecutive days. 
The assumption is that this task requires learning and therefore the mice improve their performance in each day and stay longer.
I have 80 mice, 40 of each sex, from four different genotypes.

Here's my simulation R code:

#simulation parameters
days <- 3
animals <- 80
sd <- 0.5
genotypes <- c("WT","PD","MD","BD")
sexes <- c("M","F")
wt.female.factor <- seq(1,12,4) #slope is 4
pd.female.factor <- seq(1,12,4) #slope is 4
md.female.factor <- seq(1,6,2) #slope is 2
bd.female.factor <- seq(1,3,1) #slope is 1


wt.male.factor <- seq(1,4,1.5) #slope is 1.5
pd.male.factor <- seq(1,3,1) #slope is 1
md.male.factor <- seq(1,2,1/2) #slope is 1/2
bd.male.factor <- seq(1,1+2/3,1/3) #slope is 1/3
set.seed(1)
#simulate data
sim.df <- data.frame(genotype = c(sapply(genotypes, function(g) rep(g, animals*days))),
                     animal = paste(c(sapply(genotypes, function(g) rep(g, animals*days))),sapply(1:animals, function(a) rep(a, days)),sep=""),
                     sex = rep(c(sapply(sexes, function(s) rep(s, days*animals/length(sexes)))),length(genotypes)),
                     day = rep(1:days, animals*length(genotypes)),
                     time = c(rnorm(days*animals/length(sexes),wt.male.factor,sd),rnorm(days*animals/length(sexes),wt.female.factor,sd),
                              rnorm(days*animals/length(sexes),pd.male.factor,sd),rnorm(days*animals/length(sexes),pd.female.factor,sd),
                              rnorm(days*animals/length(sexes),md.male.factor,sd),rnorm(days*animals/length(sexes),md.female.factor,sd),
                              rnorm(days*animals/length(sexes),bd.male.factor,sd),rnorm(days*animals/length(sexes),bd.female.factor,sd)),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


#convert to tabular format
sim.df.tab <- do.call("rbind",lapply(unique(sim.df$animal), function(x){
  data.frame(genotype = unique(sim.df$genotype[which(sim.df$animal == x)]),
             animal = x,
             sex = unique(sim.df$sex[which(sim.df$animal == x)]),
             day1 = sim.df$time[which(sim.df$animal == x & sim.df$day == 1)],
             day2 = sim.df$time[which(sim.df$animal == x & sim.df$day == 2)],
             day3 = sim.df$time[which(sim.df$animal == x & sim.df$day == 3)])}))


#set factors
sim.df.tab$genotype1 <- ifelse(sim.df.tab$genotype == "WT", 1, 0)
sim.df.tab$genotype2 <- ifelse(sim.df.tab$genotype == "PD", 1, 0)
sim.df.tab$genotype3 <- ifelse(sim.df.tab$genotype == "MD", 1, 0)
sim.df.tab$sex <- as.character(sim.df.tab$sex)
sim.df.tab$sex[which(sim.df.tab$sex == "M")] <- 1
sim.df.tab$sex[which(sim.df.tab$sex == "F")] <- 0
sim.df.tab$genotype1 <- as.integer(sim.df.tab$genotype1)
sim.df.tab$genotype2 <- as.integer(sim.df.tab$genotype2)
sim.df.tab$genotype3 <- as.integer(sim.df.tab$genotype3)
sim.df.tab$sex <- as.integer(sim.df.tab$sex)


#model
model <- '
i =~ 1*day1 + 1*day2 + 1*day3
s =~ 0*day1 + 1*day2 + 2*day3
# regressions
i ~ genotype1+genotype2+genotype3+sex
s ~ genotype1+genotype2+genotype3+sex
'
#fit model
fit <- growth(model, data=sim.df.tab)




As far as I can see my data are pretty straight forward so I'm puzzled why I'm getting these warnings.

Help would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Negative variances and and not positive definite covariance matrix in a growth model
parts: I'm trying to fit a growth model to my data and am getting these warnings:

Warning messages:
1: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: some estimated variances are negative
2: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.
As far as I can see my data are pretty straight forward so I'm puzzled why I'm getting these warnings.

The example data you posted only had a negative variance for the intercept, although the SE was more than 3 times larger, so you can't reject the null hypothesis that the intercept variance is nonnegative in the population.  Did you simulate the data to have a substantial variance of intercepts?  Was this the same parameter estimate that was causing the error with your real data?

Here is an enlightening article on Heywood cases:

http://dx.doi.org/10.1177/0049124112442138

Essentially, when population values are close to natural boundaries, sampling error alone could (possibly) be responsible for finite-sample estimates to be distributed across the boundary.  To test the null hypothesis that the population variance is nonnegative, you should use a bootstrap CI by setting lavaan(..., se = "bootstrap") and parameterEstimates(..., boot.ci.type = "bca.simple"), or at least use robust SEs by setting lavaan(..., se = "robust.huber.white").

Terry

Thanks a lot for your response.

This is the same error I get for my real data.

In my simulated data I meant for all factors (each genotype sex combination) to have the same intercept but differing slopes. Perhaps that the proximity of the intercept variance to zero is what's causing this - as you suggest.

However running either:
fit <- growth(model, data=sim.df.tab, se = "bootstrap")


or
fit <- growth(model, data=sim.df.tab, se = "robust.huber.white")

messages.subject: Re: Negative variances and and not positive definite covariance matrix in a growth model
parts:
Rubi,

  Let me add a little to what Terry wrote.  His suggestion was to use the robust or bootstrap standard errors to test whether your negative variance was within sampling error of zero.  You should get the same estimates, the only difference should be the method used to compute the standard errors.

  Another possibility, aside from sampling error, is that the negative variance reflects model misspecification.  Sometimes, a negative variance compensates for another aspect of a model implying excessive variance or covariance.  I notice that you simulated your data with a genotype by gender interaction in determining the slope.  For example, for females WT and PD have the same slope, but not for males, if I follow your code correctly.  However, your model contains only main effects for genotype and gender.  This misspecification might (and this is only a conjecture) explain your negative variance.

Keith
